what: REFUTED EXEMPLAR, found while closing composition-omitted-activation (III.4, 18th amendment): the-fold's source.js::blankLabelRows is byte-length-preserving but NOT sentence-COUNT-preserving on real material, which silently defeats hypergraph.js::makeRelationReader's own span-pairing check the first time organs.blankFurniture is actually wired (it had never been injected by any known caller before this pass). blankLabelRows blanks table-cell-shaped lines to spaces; on live_priors' Aristotle.txt (8000-char excerpt) this reduces spans.js::splitSentences' own sentence count from 40 to 36 by erasing terminal punctuation inside blanked cells that splitSentences was using as a boundary. makeRelationReader's pairing check (readSentences.length === originalSentences.length, guarding against a wrong address rather than risk one) then refuses every triple's span on the affected passage — measured live: 37 edges extracted, 37 edges with spans:[], 0 admitted by hyperlexicon.js's own UNADDRESSED door. The failure is silent: no exception, no warning, a passage simply loses every citation it would otherwise have earned.

reproduction.measured: text.length === blanked.length (8000 === 8000, true); splitSentences(text).length = 40; splitSentences(blanked).length = 36; first divergence at sentence index 0, where the blanked line reads as bare closing braces from a wiki template artifact
reproduction.consequence_at_call_site: hypergraph.js's own comment already states the design intent correctly ('a wrong address is worse than a coarse one') — the pairing check IS working as designed, refusing an address it cannot trust. The defect is upstream: blankLabelRows' own header calls itself length-preserving without qualifying that this means BYTE length, not the sentence-boundary count downstream callers actually depend on.

not_yet_done: no fix landed in this pass — the-fold's UNION_OMITTED declaration in live_priors/scripts/eot-digest.mjs withholds blankFurniture pending either (a) blankLabelRows preserving sentence count as well as byte count, or (b) the pairing check in hypergraph.js gaining a fallback narrower than 'refuse the whole passage' when counts disagree by a small amount
status: PARTIALLY CLOSED, 2026-09-01, same pass: the-fold/hypergraph.js was restructured so every rewrite (blankFurniture and resolvePronouns alike) applies within one already-fixed original sentence's own span, never to a whole re-split passage — the pairing check this finding names is gone entirely, by construction, not by a narrower fallback. blankFurniture itself remains withheld from live_priors' production recipe (UNION_OMITTED) pending re-measurement under the new per-sentence-safe call path; the underlying mechanism this finding convicted no longer exists to re-trigger it.
